channel.title: Clojure Backtesting
channel.description: Documentation for Clojure Backtesting, an open-source library for testing trading strategies on daily market data.

item.title: Example: Quality and Earnings
item.description: This walkthrough follows the worksheet quality_and_earnings.clj. Like the Value Strategy, it runs offline on the library's synthetic Yahoo snapshots.You will use: piotroski-signals and piotroski-f-score, fundamental-history, growth, latest-earnings, order-target-percent and get-prev-n-date.

item.title: Example: Value Strategy
item.description: This walkthrough follows the worksheet value_strategy.clj. It runs on the library's synthetic Yahoo snapshots, so it needs no network connection; open it in Gorilla REPL with make start (see Get Started), or paste the code into lein repl.You will use: build-yahoo-dataset! and load-yahoo-dataset, earnings-yield, new-period?, top-n, equal-weights, rebalance and benchmark-stats.

item.title: Yahoo Finance Data
item.description: CRSP and Compustat are the reference data for academic backtests, but they need a licence. Since version 1.1.2 the library can also use Yahoo Finance, through the clj-yfinance library: free, with no API key, for any ticker Yahoo quotes. You get daily prices with dividends and splits, plus the financial statements and earnings dates behind point-in-time fundamentals.The three steps

item.description: The functions on this page, in clojure-backtesting.fundamentals, answer one question: what did the market know about this company on the backtest date? They read the point-in-time fundamentals of a Yahoo Finance dataset, loaded with load-yahoo-dataset. item.title: Key Concepts
item.description: You do not need a finance background to use the backtester, but a few ideas come up on every page of this documentation. This page explains them once, with examples from the bundled sample dataset.What a backtest is

item.title: Automation
item.description: An automation is a condition paired with an action. The backtester checks every automation's condition on each trading day, at the end of next-date, and runs the action when the condition is true. Automations make stop-loss and take-profit orders, or any other rule, run by themselves while your strategy steps through time.The example on this page is the automation.clj worksheet, which runs on the bundled sample dataset.

item.title: Core API
item.description: These are the functions every strategy uses. The examples run on the bundled sample dataset (see Get Started), mostly with the clock at 1990-01-08. Functions for Yahoo Finance data, fundamentals and portfolio strategies have their own pages: Yahoo Finance Data, Fundamentals and Strategy Helpers.How to read this page: each function has a table of its arguments, then what it returns and an example. Arguments in [square brackets] are optional. Lines starting with => are what you type at the REPL; the lines below them are what it prints or returns.

item.title: Indicators
item.description: This page introduces the functions that calculate technical indicators. Unless stated otherwise, they calculate the indicator for the current date of the global date pointer, from the trading price (the closing price by default).The examples ran on the bundled sample dataset with the date pointer at 1990-02-19, except the second parabolic-SAR call and the ATR and keltner-channel examples, which ran on 1990-02-20, and the MACD examples, which show their own steps.

item.title: Example: Golden Cross
item.description: This walkthrough follows the worksheet golden_cross.clj. It runs on the bundled sample dataset and can be opened in Gorilla REPL with make start (see Get Started for setup).A golden cross is when a short-term moving average of a security's price crosses above a long-term one, read as a buy signal; a death cross is the opposite, the short-term average falling below the long-term one. The classic pair is the 50-day and 200-day averages. The sample data covers only January to March 1990, so the worksheet uses 15-day and 30-day averages instead, on securities 10001 ("AAA") and 10002 ("BBB").

item.title: Example: Fundamental Analysis
item.description: This walkthrough follows the worksheet Fundamental analysis.clj. It runs on the bundled sample dataset and can be opened in Gorilla REPL with make start (see Get Started for setup).It implements a simple fundamental analysis strategy: rank securities by return on equity (ROE) from their quarterly filings and buy the best one.

item.title: Example: Buying on Margin
item.description: This walkthrough follows the worksheet buying_on_margin.clj. It runs on the bundled sample dataset and can be opened in Gorilla REPL with make start (see Get Started for setup).It shows how the backtester handles trading with and without leverage, the initial and maintenance margin requirements, and short selling. All trades use security 10001 ("AAA"), which trades at about $50 in the sample data. Orders fill at the next trading day's close.
